## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason about tenancy guardrails using Kubernetes primitives and a minimal webhook, aligning with CNF gateway multi-tenant constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes ResourceQuota
- LimitRange
- ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
- Per-tenant policy mapping

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-quota
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.cpu: "8"
    limits.memory: 16Gi
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-limit
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: "500m"
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "250m"
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy-as-code proficiency, practical use of Gatekeeper/OPA, and ability to derive concrete manifests and validation steps for a CNF multi-tenant setup.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, hostNetwork, and Privileged security controls
- Namespace-scoped policy targeting CNFs
- Lightweight test manifests to validate allow/deny paths

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: cnfnamespacesecurity.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: cnf-a-security
spec:
  namespace: cnf-a
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-cnf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      privileged: false
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# Non-compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-cnf
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      privileged: true
```

## Follow-up Steps

- Apply ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, and test manifests in a single namespace and observe denial events for non-compliant pods.
- Extend with a quick kubectl patch to simulate remediation and re-validate.

```javascript
function evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) {

    if (r.method === method && (r.path === path || matches(r.path, path))) return true
  }
  return false
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses real-world upgrade discipline in cloud-native networking functions (CNF): zero-downtime deployments, per-tenant TLS key rotation, and reliable KMS-backed certificate flows—all in a multi-tenant Kubernetes environment.

## Key Concepts
- Canary rollouts with per-namespace traffic control using progressive traffic shifting
- CSR-based TLS rotation via an in-cluster KMS-backed Certificate Authority
- TenantRotation CRD to trigger cross-namespace certificate refresh
- Readiness probes with TLS handshake validation during upgrades
- Traffic shadows for testing new versions without affecting production

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```

```yaml
# Example 2: TenantRotation CRD for per-tenant TLS rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-mtls-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: tenant-a-mtls-secret
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 12h
  issuerRef:
    name: kms-tenant-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
  commonName: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: security.example.com/v1
kind: TenantRotation
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rotation
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenantNamespace: tenant-a
  certificateRef:
    name: tenant-mtls-cert
  rotationStrategy: rolling
  preRotationValidation:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 30s
```

```yaml
# Example 3: Minimal one-namespace test manifest

  name: test-tenant
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-ca-key

type: Opaque

  ca.key: <base64-encoded-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: test-ca-issuer
```

- **Canary deployments**: Gradually shift traffic between versions to validate changes safely

- **Weight-based traffic splitting**: Distribute traffic percentages across subsets

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-dr
spec:
  host: cnf-gateway
  subsets:
  - name: prod
    labels:
      version: prod
  - name: canary
    labels:
      version: canary
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-vs
spec:
  hosts:
  - cnf-gateway
  http:
  - match:
    - headers:
        x-tenant-id:
          exact: canary
    route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: canary
      weight: 15
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: prod
      weight: 85
  - route:
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests multi-cloud KMS integration, cross-tenant isolation, and downtime-free key rotation in CNF provenance.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-cloud KMS integration (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSM)
- Cosign-based signing, SBOM binding, provenance store consistency
- Runtime attestation enforcement during rotation
- Rollback and rollback-triggered validation

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo-shell: rotate key in each KMS, re-sign images, publish new SBOM
cosign generate-key-pair -kms aws-kms:alias/cnfsign
cosign sign --key kms:aws:kms:alias/cnfsign <image>
cosign verify <image>
# sign SBOM and publish provenance
sbom-tool attach --image <image> --sbom sbom.json
provenance-store.push <image> <sbom.json> --kms-rotation
```
